title: KV locality splay reservation and prefill-window coordinator
creator: Aisha Mukherjee
description: Reduce decode tail latency and tenant interference by introducing a small reservation splay and a coordinated prefill-window controller that biases allocations toward tenant-local hot segments and smooths reservation handoff during bursty traffic.
background: Current paged KV allocation treats all incoming prefill requests equally which leads to frequent cross-tenant eviction churn under bursty workloads. Observed effects: long tail latencies during mixed-tenant microbursts, noisy neighbor eviction of recently-warmed segments, and suboptimal kernel packing due to fragmented hotsets.
goals: Decrease 95th/99th token decode latency for mixed-tenant workloads by 15-25%
Reduce cross-tenant eviction rate and unnecessary restore work by 30%
Maintain or improve average token throughput and avoid regression for single-tenant steady workloads
proposal_summary: Introduce: (1) a per-tenant reservation splay (small soft-reserve credit) that biases page allocation toward tenant-local fragments; (2) a prefill-window coordinator that groups prefill admission into short epochs to avoid interleaved thrash; (3) lightweight metadata for 'stickiness' that prefers reuse of recently-warmed microsegments when kernel packing suggests benefit.
detailed_design: Reservation splay: each tenant receives a soft credit bucket (measured in microsegments) that can be consumed preferentially for new prefill allocations. Credits decay exponentially with inactivity to avoid long-term starvation.

Prefill-window coordinator: requests are bucketed into 50ms windows per shard. During a window, prefill admissions are sequenced to maximize locality: prefer allocations that co-locate with current decoding kernels and warm KV ranges.
Stickiness metadata: maintain a 4-bit recency counter per microsegment to bias selection for reuse; counters saturate and decay on read/write cycles to avoid permanent favoritism.

Admission policy: if shard free pages below low-watermark, coordinator throttles admission and prefers reuse/compaction hints instead of new allocations. A fast-path bypass exists for P0 customer tokens.
Kernel hinting: provide kernel-selection hints (coalesced vs split) to the allocator so it can align microsegment placements with upcoming decode kernel expectations to reduce kernel-switch overhead.
Telemetry: emit per-window metrics (prefill_admitted, prefill_throttled, eviction_cross_tenant_pct, reservation_hit_rate) for dashboards and alerting thresholds.
tradeoffs: Soft reservations improve locality but add bookkeeping and slightly reduce global packing efficiency if not tuned.
Prefill-window epochs introduce small added latency to admission (tens of ms) but reduce decode tail by preventing concurrent thrash that costs hundreds of ms in restore.
Stickiness metadata increases memory footprint per microsegment (~2-4 bytes) which must be justified by reduced restore work.
Bypass rules for P0 tokens complicate admission logic and require careful auditing for fairness.
Kernel hinting couples allocator decisions to model/kernel predictions; misprediction could worsen packing and require fallback policies.
implementation_steps: Design proto: implement reservation splay counters and window coordinator in allocator simulator (local branch) - Aisha
Simulate: run mixed-tenant microburst synthetic workloads using existing kv-sim harness and compare baseline vs splay+window - Daniel
Benchmark: capture 50/95/99 token latency and eviction rates across varying shard loads (25/50/75/95%) - Daniel
Integrate: add stickiness metadata to allocator store with compact representation; expose kernel hint API to runtime - Eng pair
Feature flag: gate new behavior behind 'kv_locality_splay' rollout flag and defaults off in prod shards
Canary: enable on dedicated test clusters with representative tenant mix and monitor dashboards for regressions
Rollout: staged rollout to low-risk shards, then to medium, then global if metrics agree
Cleanup: remove simulator scaffolding and reconcile config surfaces in console
benchmarks: Simulator run ID: sim-20250226-014 (mixed-tenant flash bursts)
Baseline eviction cross-tenant: 18.4% of evictions, new: 12.3% (-33%)
Memory overhead: +3.1% for stickiness metadata in microsegment table
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: kv.prefill_throttled_rate > 5% for 5m => investigate admission choking
Alert: kv.eviction_cross_tenant_pct spikes > 25% relative to baseline => rollback flag
SLOs: keep tail decode 99th within 10% of canary baseline during rollout
rollout_plan: Feature flag development and internal canary (2 shards) - week 1
Extended canary with 10 production-like shards and close SRE monitoring - week 2
Gradual ramp to 30% of shards with auto-abort on alert triggers - week 3
Full rollout after stability window and leadership sign-off - week 4
acceptance_criteria: Metrics: 95th token latency reduced >=15% and eviction cross-tenant reduced >=25% in canary compared to baseline
No regression in average throughput (> -5%) or memory blowups (> +8% memory on shard)
Code reviewed and security review completed for bypass logic
Feature flag supports instant disable with safe draining policy
testing: Unit tests for reservation counter edge cases and decay semantics
Integration test: prefill-window sequencing under simulated multi-tenant bursts
Load test: end-to-end smoke with kernels that exercise kernel-hint alignments
Chaos test: simulate allocator process restart and verify reservation recovery
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: miscalibrated window size can add admission latency - Mitigation: add dynamic tuning to shrink/grow window based on request burstiness
Risk: reservation starvation for long-tail tenants - Mitigation: decay curve with minimum guarantee and emergency bypass for fairness
Risk: increased memory for metadata - Mitigation: compact 4-bit counter packing and opt-out for tiny shards
